failure_summary.description: Answer unparseable (n_pred=0). Lines ended `], "},`, so the `optional parameters` key was dropped mid-write, or the final `]` before `</answer>` was missing (gaming:15, music:7, ecommerce:19). The first two also used `Provider — X: X` names.
Schema says `Required parameters: none`, but the main entity or ID went into `required parameters` (Genius Videos `artist_id`, Zelda games list `name`).

Named retailer dropped or wrong sibling chosen. Aliexpress was missing from the 'compare retailers' query (ecommerce:177). The price-range plus free-shipping query went to Shopee with an invalid `site` enum value instead of Aliexpress Item Search 2 (ecommerce:19). The MX clause used `Email API: Check Email MX Records` instead of the Email Existence Validator MX tool (email:32).
Optionals the query implies were omitted or mis-cased: Asos `lang`, chess `count`, card `value`=A, lowercase `region`=us / Pokedex values.

patch.reasoning: Three of eight trajectories scored zero because the answer did not parse. In each, the model wrote `], "},` or dropped the final `]` instead of a complete `"optional parameters": [...]},` ending. The skill has plenty of 'never repeat the key' warnings but no literal line shape to imitate, and those warnings may be pushing the model to truncate the key. Edit 1 adds three canonical line templates covering the empty, required-only and optional-only shapes, and shows the bad ending once. Edit 2 strengthens the 'Required: none -> []' rule, which was violated twice, with concrete schema-specific cases. Edit 3 covers the two ecommerce retailer and tool-choice misses, using schema facts only. Edit 4 fixes the MX sibling choice, which has a consistent gold preference.

edits.target: - The answer is one flat, bracket-balanced list `[{...}, {...}]` inside `<answer>` tags. Do not close the list early or leave stray brackets.
edits.content:
- LINE TEMPLATES (copy the shape exactly; every call line has all three keys and ends `]},`):
  - required only: `{"tool name": "Shazam: songs/get-count", "required parameters": [{"name": "key", "value": "40333609"}], "optional parameters": []},`
  - optional only: `{"tool name": "Genius - Song Lyrics: Videos", "required parameters": [], "optional parameters": [{"name": "artist_id", "value": "16775"}, {"name": "per_page", "value": "15"}]},`
  - The LAST call line ends `]}` with no comma, and the next line is `]</answer>` (the closing `]` is never omitted).
  - A call line must never end in `"},`, `"}` or `], "},`. That is a half-written `optional parameters` key (real zero-score output: `"required parameters": [{"name": "key", "value": "40333609"}], "},`). Always write the full `"optional parameters": [...]` and then `}`. Names are always `Provider: Endpoint` from the `### ` heading, never `Provider — X: X`.

(e.g. CheapShark `title`, `limit`; Flight Info `FlightNumber`; `Genius - Song Lyrics: Videos` `artist_id`, `per_page`; `The Legend of Zelda: List of The Legend of Zelda games` `name`, `limit`). This holds even when the value is the call's main entity or ID. Before writing each call, read its `Required parameters:` line: if it says `none`, write `"required parameters": []` first and put every value in the optional list.

- NAMED RETAILERS AND SHOPPING FILTERS. A 'compare across BestBuy, Wayfair, Zappos and Aliexpress' clause needs a search call for each retailer that has a keyword-search tool, so do not drop Aliexpress (`Aliexpress DataHub: Aliexpress - Item Search 2`, optional `q`, `region`=`US`, `currency`=`USD`, `page`=`1`) or BestBuy (`keyword`, `page`). A product search with a price range and 'free shipping' needs the tool whose optionals include `startPrice`, `endPrice` and `switches` (`Aliexpress DataHub: Aliexpress - Item Search 2`: startPrice=`600`, endPrice=`900`, `switches`=`freeShipping`). 'Some iPhone accessories' is a separate `Aliexpress DataHub: Aliexpress - Item Search` call with `q`. Never put a value outside an ENUM's listed options into a required param (Shopee `site` accepts only my/th/vn/ph/sg/id/tw/br, so `US` is invalid and that tool cannot serve a US query).

'MX records' -> the MX tool, and when `Email Existence Validator: Get the MX Records` is listed use it (not `Email API: Check Email MX Records`). The same query's disposable clause then also uses `Email Existence Validator: Check for Disposable emails`.
